findings: Database tests mutate external rename fixtures: rename/move file/directory/archive and restore on normal success. They verify selected paths/counts and file ids, but do not inject SQL/commit failure after filesystem movement, transaction rollback or crash recovery. Do not execute on user media.

testMoveZipped actually calls rename, same as testRenameZipped, so its name is not proof of archive-member move coverage. existingPaths assumes fixtures provide two suitable paths; no explicit precondition assertion there.

Negative-match test deliberately asserts order-dependent filtering: group[a,b,c] becomes empty while[b,c,a] retains[b,c] with negative a-b/a-c relationships. It checks symmetry after reload, but this is not order-independent graph partitioning.

Weed tests assert directional relationships, rejection when original already weed, orphan invalidation after database removal and restoration after re-add, and reload after weed removal. No append/write failure, Unicode-map persistence or concurrent-writer test present.

Path tests explicitly expect file.ZiP not an archive while lower/uppercase ZIP are archives. Mixed-case exclusion is part of fixtures rather than a tested all-case extension invariant. Archive member strings are lexical examples, not actual archive load/CRC/decode tests.

testpath parseArchive_benchmark is declared ordinary private method, not private Q_SLOT, while data helper is slot. No inference that QTest invokes the benchmark body; source labels alone are not timing evidence.

Archive member data repeats identical ..zip:z tag. Whether Qt rejects duplicate tags was not executed. Windows-looking paths appear in benchmark data only, not proof of native Windows filesystem behavior.
